subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Kirchhoff's Current Law
description: A 60-second lesson on Kirchhoff's Current Law.

hook.text: At any junction in a circuit, current in equals current out. None is lost.

buildup.text: If 5 amps flow into a node and 3 amps leave one branch, 2 amps leave the other.

discovery.text: This is charge conservation — electrons don't pile up or vanish at a junction.

twist.text: KCL works even in circuits with thousands of nodes. Every node must balance.

climax.text: Together, KVL and KCL let you solve any linear circuit completely.

punchline.text: What flows in must flow out. Charge has nowhere to hide.

quiz.question: What does Kirchhoff's Current Law require at a junction?
options: Voltage must be the same on all branches
Total current entering must equal total current leaving
Each branch must carry equal current
